Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic disrupted higher education globally, spurring universities to swiftly adopt non-traditional remote teaching methods. A primary outcome was a surge in Flash-based educational videos, which, despite initial concerns, garnered widespread popularity among students. Drawing on a dataset of 955 videos, we examined the educational outcomes associated with Flash instruction versus remote and in-person classes. Our findings indicate that students utilizing Flash videos scored significantly higher than those in remote or traditional classroom settings. Specifically, scores from students instructed primarily via Flash exceeded remote learning scores by 0.22 standard deviations (SD) and traditional in-person scores by 0.37 SD. Ultimately, we attribute this discrepancy to variations in instructional quality and the widespread application of active learning strategies within these popular Flash video curricula.
